Register a lag sequential analysis engine

Source: R/engine-registry.R
register_lsa_engine.Rd

register_lsa_engine() adds a lag sequential analysis engine under a name, after which lsa(data, engine = name) fits it; the fit is read, resampled and plotted like any other. An engine is the part of a lag sequential analysis that turns a table of observed transitions into expected counts and cell-wise tests. The built-in engines implement the classical analysis of Bakeman and Quera (1995), a two-cell test, Sackett's (1979) bidirectional test, and the parallel and non-parallel dominance tests (Wampold, 1984). Other tests of the same table, such as a different residual or a model-based expectation, can be added as engines and then used with every function of the package.

Re-registering a name replaces the engine for the session. The built-in engines are registered when the package loads.

Usage

register_lsa_engine(name, fn, description, requires = character())

Arguments

name

Name of the engine, used as lsa(engine = name).

fn

The engine function. It is called with transitions (the lsa_transitions() object), structural_zeros (NULL or a K x K 0/1 matrix), alternative, n_events (NULL for transition-matrix input) and any engine parameters given to lsa(), so it should accept transitions and .... It must return a named list holding at least the K x K matrices obs, exp, prob, adj_res and p; further K x K matrices become extra columns of transitions().

description

One-line description shown by list_lsa_engines().

requires

Names of packages the engine needs (default none); lsa() checks that they are installed before fitting.

Value

name, invisibly.

Conditions

Errors carry the class lagdynamics_error and lagdynamics_bad_input when fn has no transitions argument.

References

Bakeman, R., & Quera, V. (1995). Analyzing interaction: Sequential analysis with SDIS and GSEQ. Cambridge University Press.

Sackett, G. P. (1979). The lag sequential analysis of contingency and cyclicity in behavioral interaction research. In J. D. Osofsky (Ed.), Handbook of infant development (pp. 623-649). Wiley.

Wampold, B. E. (1984). Tests of dominance in sequential categorical data. Psychological Bulletin, 96(2), 424-429.

See also

list_lsa_engines(), get_lsa_engine(), unregister_lsa_engine(), lsa()

Examples

# An engine that tests Pearson residuals under independence
pearson_engine <- function(transitions, ...) {
  obs <- transitions$obs
  expected <- outer(rowSums(obs), colSums(obs)) / sum(obs)
  residual <- (obs - expected) / sqrt(expected)
  list(obs = obs, exp = expected, prob = obs / rowSums(obs),
       adj_res = residual, p = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(residual)))
}
register_lsa_engine("pearson", pearson_engine,
                    description = "Pearson residuals under independence")
list_lsa_engines()
#>                    name
#> 1         bidirectional
#> 2             classical
#> 3 nonparallel_dominance
#> 4    parallel_dominance
#> 5               pearson
#> 6              two_cell
#>                                                            description requires
#> 1 Sackett's bidirectional / matched-pair test on the symmetrized table         
#> 2                    Bakeman & Quera classical lag sequential analysis         
#> 3       Sackett's non-parallel-dominance (observed-SE + binomial) test         
#> 4                      Sackett's parallel-dominance (expected-SE) test         
#> 5                                 Pearson residuals under independence         
#> 6                  2x2 cell test (odds ratio, log-OR Wald z, Yule's Q)         
fit <- lsa(engagement, engine = "pearson")
transitions(fit, significant = TRUE)
#>         from         to lag count  expected       prob   prob_col   adj_res
#> 1     Active     Active   1   459 247.03460 0.69756839 0.70506912 13.486091

#> 4     Active    Average   1   176 289.53518 0.26747720 0.23066841 -6.672365
#> 5    Average    Average   1   458 330.45732 0.60985353 0.60026212  7.016133
#> 6     Active Disengaged   1    23 121.43022 0.03495441 0.07187500 -8.932336
#> 7 Disengaged Disengaged   1   157  59.97693 0.48307692 0.49062500 12.528033

unregister_lsa_engine("pearson")
